notes: Stratification screen, declared at the 2026-07-27 huddle BEFORE the shift split was tabulated: if evening's defect mix differed from day's, the causes would be people-shaped (training, handover) and the fix would have to split by shift. Declared as its own single question with its own single test -- the project's pre-declared primary comparison is the before/after proportion test (print-hyp-beforeafter), and this screen is not it, hence declared_primary false. Input is the check sheet's own table: failed-check marks by type and shift, both from the same to-dataset export the Pareto ran on. Cochran's rule is checked by the engine before it will compute (one light cell is within the rule; the route echo shows the check). Verdict: no association shown -- the defect mix is the same process on both shifts, which routes the fix at the process, not at a shift.

question.question_text: Baseline window, failed-check marks by defect type and shift: is the defect-type mix associated with shift (day vs evening)?

routing.question: Baseline window, failed-check marks by defect type and shift: is the defect-type mix associated with shift (day vs evening)?

decision_path.answer: 88% of cells have expected>=5 (need >=80%); smallest expected cell=3.95 (need >=1)

value.effect_size_ci_method: not computed -- no simple closed-form CI for Cramer's V (a bootstrap or noncentral-chi-square CI is out of scope for this v1 route); the point estimate is reported plainly.
assumptions_checked: Cochran's rule cleared before this test ran (matrix §4a EXIT-07): >= 80% of cells expected >= 5, no cell expected < 1
counts are independent observations (one per unit, not repeated measures)

plain_language.comparison_summary: Tested whether the row categories (Trim misalignment, Wrong paper stock, Ink smudge / banding, Wrong quantity) and column categories (Day shift, Evening shift) are associated -- a 4x2 contingency table, n=139, chi-square test of independence.
plain_language.p_value_meaning: p = 0.8948, at or above the alpha=0.05 threshold: no difference shown at this sample size. That is not proof there is no difference, and it is not the same claim as 'no difference exists' -- a smaller true difference, or the same difference measured with more data, could still turn up significant.
plain_language.effect_size_in_words: Cramer's V = 0.066 -- a negligible association between the row and column categories (0 = no association, 1 = perfect association).
plain_language.practical_significance_prompt: Statistically detectable ≠ big enough to matter -- compare the effect size above against the goal.

provenance.method: Pearson chi-square test of independence (Pearson 1900; no Yates continuity correction -- standard practice for r x c tables, applied uniformly here) + Cramer's V = sqrt(chi2/(n*(min(r,c)-1)))
